page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-90 is a general-purpose server instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 90 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 45 physical AMD EPYC 9B14 cores with multithreading enabled. The system is equipped with 360 GB of RAM, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

The AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, which accelerate vector and neural network operations. Cryptographic tasks are accelerated via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instructions. Integer and bit manipulation capabilities are supported by BMI2, ADX, and FMA flags. Virtualization and security features include hypervisor support, IBRS, and SSBD.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, software compilation with Clang, and Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions and encryption. Strong performance is observed in single-core CPU tasks, memory bandwidth for read operations, and database operations. However, memory write bandwidth for large blocks and single-threaded gzip compression fall into the average performance tier.

Given its high core density and balanced memory-to-CPU ratio, this instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference prompt processing. The dedicated hardware allocation offers reliable resource density, though the absence of local storage requires external block storage attachment for persistent data.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-90 is a general-purpose server instance featuring 90 dedicated vCPUs and 360 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 45 physical cores with multithreading, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache. The CPU includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and SHA_NI for vector math and cryptography. Benchmarks show top-tier multi-core CPU performance, software compilation speeds, and encryption capabilities, alongside strong database and static web serving throughput. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs, making it a highly capable option for compute-heavy, non-accelerated workloads. It is well-suited for large-scale software development pipelines, database hosting, and text processing tasks requiring high multi-threaded performance.
